reason: The text portrays Moses as a positive leader who responds to fearful and complaining Israelites with reassurance and faith-based guidance (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה אַל־ תִּירָאוּ הִֽתְיַצְב֗וּ וּרְאוּ אֶת־ יְשׁוּעַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה - 'Do not fear, stand still and see the salvation of the Lord'). He does not employ violence against his own people despite their fear and complaints. In contrast, the text shows God directing violence against the external enemy (Egypt). The exemplary leadership model presented is one of steadfast faith, moral authority, and trust in divine protection—not violence against unruly people within one's community.
